messages:
marta: Heads-up — CI job `eval-runner/embeddings-rerank` started failing after the quantize branch merge. NDCG numbers dropped ~0.12 on the nightly, and the rerank-runner log shows some weird top-k ordering. Anyone seen this?
ci-bot: [eval-runner/embeddings-rerank] Job failed: exit status 2. Logs: /ci/artifacts/1789001234/runner.log
sunil: dropping the log here — see the metric block and the sorter warning around line 412.
```
WARNING: unstable sort detected for scores at indices [23,24,25]
File: rerank/runner/metrics.py:412
Trace: ValueError: ideal_dcg is zero
```
oliver: hmm ValueError ideal_dcg zero indicates the IDCG normalization path got 0. That usually happens when the relevance labels for the query are all zeros or duplicates messed up the pooling. Did the test data change?
kai: short note — the quantize changes cast embeddings to int8 in some paths; when we compute dot-product we convert back to float but precision loss can create exact ties more often. Ties -> unstable sort -> different ranking -> IDCG calculation could end up zero if expected rels all zero.
jess: i reproduced locally with the new fixture: `pytest tests/runner/test_rerank_metrics.py::test_ndcg_pipeline -k quantize -q` and I see duplicate doc ids in the generated candidate pool. That will force ideal_dcg to compute with duplicate candidates and our IDCG code currently dedupes by position, resulting in 0 for some queries.
oliver: can you paste the small failing example export?
jess: sure — here's a minimized repro (ids anonymized):
```
query: q_314
candidates: [doc_1(rel=0), doc_1(rel=0), doc_2(rel=0)]
expected_topk: [doc_2, doc_1]
```
marta: that duplicate doc_1 is coming from the mteb-ish sampler we added for diversity. We added a path that merges corpus slices but didn't uniq by doc_id. My bad.
sunil: two fixes then: 1) dedupe candidate pool by doc_id in the runner before scoring (cheap), 2) make metric defensive: if ideal_dcg == 0 then return 0.0 and log context.
oliver: agreed. Also add a stable tie-breaker in the sorter: sort by (score, doc_id) descending so quantize-induced equal scores are deterministic. Example change: `sorted(cands, key=lambda x: (x.score, x.doc_id), reverse=True)`. That avoids unstable sort warnings.
kai: small caveat — doc_id tie-breaker changes ranking slightly vs before, but determinism is more important for CI. We should note this in changelog and dashboards.
jess: pushing a branch: `fix/runner-dedupe-stable-sort`. Patch includes:
```
- scores_sorted = sorted(cands, key=lambda x: x.score, reverse=True)
+ scores_sorted = sorted(cands, key=lambda x: (x.score, x.doc_id), reverse=True)
+ # ensure unique candidate ids to avoid zero IDCGs in evals
+ seen = set()
+ uniq_cands = [c for c in scores_sorted if not (c.doc_id in seen or seen.add(c.doc_id))]
```
marta: great. also added a defensive check in metrics.py: if ideal_dcg <= 0: log.debug("zero ideal_dcg", query_id=query.id, rels=relevance_list) and return 0.0.
ci-bot: running `pytest tests/runner/test_rerank_metrics.py::test_ndcg_pipeline -q` on branch fix/runner-dedupe-stable-sort
ci-bot: run passed locally on CI container (python3.10, cuda mock) — N=1
sunil: can we add a tiny unit test to assert stability under equal scores? Eg create 3 candidates with identical scores but different ids and assert deterministic ordering after the stable sort.
oliver: yes, add `tests/unit/test_sorting.py::test_stable_tiebreaker` and one integration test `test_runner_handles_duplicate_ids`. Keep both very small.
kai: one more: update the telemetry to emit a `runner.tiebreaker_in_use` metric when doc_id tiebreaker is used so we can measure how often quantize causes ties in production.
jess: added telemetry ping in commit and a quick dashboard tile in perf/rerank: "tie frequency" (30d). Also added CI job retry policy for flaky eval tests: only rerun the single failing job once instead of the whole pipeline. See .github/workflows/eval.yml snippet I pushed.
marta: deployed patch to staging and re-ran the nightly eval — NDCG returned to expected baseline ±0.01. :party-parrot: We'll keep the quantize branch in staging and observe 48h, then merge to main.
sunil: thanks all — can one of you open the release PR and tag `v0.9.3-evalfix`? I can fast-track the canary once merged.
oliver: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rerank/pull/532 :eyes: includes changelog, tests, and CI tweaks.
marta: closing loop: doc note added to onboarding docs explaining that candidate pools must be deduped and that metric normalization expects unique doc ids. Also added a short note in eval-harness README about quantization tie effects.
ci-bot: thread archived after successful merge to main at 1789001302."
